name: Manassas National Battlefield Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Manassas National Battlefield Park in Prince William County, Virginia, preserves the site of two major Civil War battles. The First Battle of Bull Run (Manassas) on July 21, 1861, was the war's first major land engagement, shattering both sides' expectations of a quick conflict and earning Confederate General Thomas J. Jackson his famous nickname "Stonewall." The Second Battle of Manassas, fought August 28–30, 1862, was a decisive Confederate victory that brought Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia to the doorstep of Washington, D.C. and set the stage for Lee's first invasion of the North. The battlefield was designated a national battlefield park in 1940 and preserves approximately 5,000 acres of the historic landscape.
